9.0     Roll Cooling Water System

The Roll cooling water system is designed to prevent damage to the rolls and delivery guides from the hot
product traveling through the mill. The flow rate to each location is adjusted by manual valves. Water
ON/OFF is controlled by Water Cooling single solenoid valve. Energizing the solenoid turns water on to the
mill. De-energizing the solenoid turns water off. The solenoid valve is energized whenever the pinch roll
motor is running above 7% of normal speed.

The Water Cooling Pressure switch indicates when the correct water pressure is present. If the logic
indicates that water should be on and there is no pressure switch signal, an alarm is initiated. If the
condition continues for 10 seconds, the C&D shear SCRAP CUT function is initiated and billet delivery is
halted. A fault message is displayed to the operator.

10.0    Lubrication

The pinch roll receives lubrication from the mill lubrication system. The Lube Pressure switch initiates an
alarm if lube pressure not correct. Correct lube pressure is a permissive requirement to start pinch rolls drive.
LOW lube pressure signal causes the following to occur:

        After the pinch roll is running and a LOW pressure condition occurs, a 0.5 second time delay is
        initiated. If the LOW pressure condition is present after the time delay ends, the following functions
        take place:

        a.   The "scrap cut" mode for the C&D shear at the entry to the NTM® is initiated to divert the
             stock to the scrap chopping shear.

        b.   Once product has cleared the pinch roll and laying head as indicated by the tracking system,
             the pinch roll drive is fast stopped.

A Water Sensor is located in the pinch roll and laying head return line. If water is detected, an alarm
condition is indicated to the operator.

11.0    Speed Calibration

The maximum and minimum pinch roll diameter and groove details are listed in the Morgan reference
drawings. Speed calibration is based on the effective diameter at the bottom of the groove. Refer to reference
drawings for details.

12.0    Pinch Roll Gap

Two screws on the top of pinch roll are used to set the limit for maximum roll open position and the limit
for minimum roll close position.

Roll Open Gap 10 mm.
Roll Close gap 0.5 mm for all sizes.

STANDARD OPERATION
Important: Make sure all safety guards are in place and interlocks are set before operating mill
equipment. NEVER By-Pass Interlock Systems
1.0     Pinch Roll Opening and Closing

The opening and closing of the pinch rolls is operated by the pinch Servomotor and controlled by pinch Servo
Drive.

When the first time the servo drive power on or size change or manual open, the pinch roll will open slowly to
touch the mechanical stop, then close 1mm to calibrate the resolver reference position.

The pinch roll will close to touch the material after getting Pinch Roll Close signal by tracking system. Pinch
force or torque is maintained by applying constant torque or current to the servo motor while the pinch roll is
in the pinching position.

The control will memorize and update the pinching position while pinch roll is closed and pinching torque is
stable in auto mode. Also the control will set the pre-pinch position (pinching position - 4 mm) and max pinch
position (pinching position + 3 mm) for the next billet.

The pinch roll is closed when the head end is just passing and maintains the pinch torque as operator setting in
auto mode.

CD/HMD1 located ahead of CD Shear is used to initiate tracking to close the pinch rolls on tail ends in auto
mode. Tail end at pinch roll opens rolls to pre-pinch position in auto mode.

There are two pinch torque settings:

        LOW pinch torque is used when rolls are closed on rod.

        HIGH pinch torque is used on tail ends during speedup or stepdown. High pinch torque assists in
        gripping rod and also prevents rolls from opening due to product force.

Refer to the separate section in this document for typical settings of LOW and HIGH pinch torque.

Pinch torque is remotely adjustable in the main pulpit by two settings which are switched in the PLC logic.


2.0     Pinch Roll Slipping and Trouble Shooting

Pinch roll slip is a function of incorrect low air pressure value and/or incorrect speed values. Incorrect speed
can be the result of either, too high over speed or too high of a tension setting.

It is easier to trouble shoot pinch roll problems if the pinch roll mode selection is made for continuous pinch.
This enables the operator to monitor the performance of the pinch roll for a long period at low pressure, a
slipping condition can then be easily identified and rectified.

3. The % tension setting should be in the ranges indicated in Table 2. Check that when the pinch rolls are

4. Assuming that the condition for items 1 & 2 are correct, then by gradually reducing the tension setting,

The Pinch Roll is designed for manual and automatic operation. Operating stations (Main Pulpit and Local Control

Note: For efficient operation of the pinch roll assembly operators are required to constantly monitor all
components and control systems.

                  down.

Intelligent Pinch Roll                                                                                         Operation and
At Laying Head                                                                                        Maintenance Instructions
CLEANLINESS
Cleanliness is the highest priority when mounting the rolls on the roll shafts. If dirt is present on the roll,
sleeve and shaft assembly the wear process on the tapered sleeve and the roll pinion shaft is rapidly
accelerated. As the taper on the shaft and sleeve wear the amount of contact between the two surfaces
decreases, eventually decreasing the amount of torque that can be transmitted and increasing the likelihood
of roll slippage or breakage. To achieve the best results it is necessary to clean the pinion shaft tapers every
time a roll is changed. Any oil residue should be removed by using non- petroleum based cleaning fluid.
Clean, lint free type cleaning cloths should be used.

IMPORTANT: Always use a new cloth to help prevent the shaft tapers from damage by debris and
particles in cloth acting as an abrasive.

If a roll is removed and then remounted on the mill without going to the roll shop, then the bore of the roll
and the tapered sleeve should be cleaned before they are reassembled. The pinion shaft taper must also be
cleaned as well as both faces of the roll as it is important that the roll contacts the flinger or the spacers,
squarely. If dirt gets between the flinger and roll face or spacer then this can damage the roll neck seals as
well as cause axial misalignment.

USING SPACERS
Carbide rolls can have between 1 and 4 grooves cut in the barrel depending on the width of the groove and
the width of the roll

In order to maintain a constant pass centerline a spacer must be mounted between the roll face and flinger
when using the outside grooves on a multi-groove roll. When placing the roll assembly onto the roll shaft
ensure that the spacer is squarely positioned between the flinger and drive side roll face. When using the
inside grooves on a multi-groove roll the spacer must be mounted on the work side of the roll face.

IMPORTANT: Always reference the running arrangement drawings provided with the equipment to
ensure that the correct parts are used for each roll assembly.

    4.1          Roll Mounting

                 A. Ensure the roll shafts are at operating temperature prior to mounting any rolls.

                      IMPORTANT: If rolls are mounted on cold shafts then they will be difficult to
                      remove after rolling when the shafts are warm.

                 B. Release the entry and delivery side guides, if they are mounted on the housing and
                    remove them.

                 C. Clean the roll shafts thoroughly using Scotch-Brite and a non-petroleum-based solvent
                    to remove all dirt and oil film. Ensure the cleaning cloth used is clean and lint free.

                 D. Ensure that the flinger is clean and seated correctly.

                 E. Carefully place the roll assembly onto the shaft. Take care not to introduce dirt during
                    this procedure. If the operator wears gloves they should be clean, as should the
                    operators hands if gloves are not worn.
By Morgan Construction Co.                                                                                    Page 23
15 Belmont Street, Worcester, MA 01605                                                                          Rev A
www.morganco.com
                                      Copyright © Morgan Construction Company   All Rights Reserved

records.source_file: Ch 21 Vizag Pinchroll at Laying Head.pdf

Intelligent Pinch Roll                                                                                      Operation and
At Laying Head                                                                                     Maintenance Instructions

              F. Check that the roll is correctly (seated squarely) positioned against the flinger.

              G. Screw the mounting tool onto the roll shaft until it is hand tight against the face of the
                 roll then back off the mounting tool 1/8 turn. This will prevent the tool from sticking
                 after mounting.

                   IMPORTANT: If the inner piston is not fully retracted then the outer piston will
                   not contact the roll face. If this procedure is continued with the inner cylinder not
                   fully retracted then the outer cylinder seal will be blown and the tool must be
                   repaired.

              H. Connect the two hoses to the correct nipples. Note the hose connections are male and
                 female preventing incorrect connection to the tool.

              I.   Switch ON the pump unit at the front mounted ON \ OFF switch.

              J.   On the pump unit remote control box, turn the switch to "MOUNT", release the red
                   push button marked "PULL TO START"

              K. Press the “MOUNT” push button on the remote control box. The following sequence
                 should occur:

                   •   Piston # 1 is pressurized to hold the roll in position against the flinger.
                   •   Piston #2 is also pressurized to press the tapered sleeve into the roll until the
                       pressure increases on both pistons.

                   Note: Before releasing the “MOUNT” pushbutton, check that the pressures on both
                   pistons have reached the set pressure.

              L. Release the “MOUNT” push button on the remote control box. The following
                 sequence should occur:
                 • Piston # 2 is released immediately and is pushed back to its home position.
                 • Piston # 1 is released only after a preset time, initially set to 30 seconds. The
                     piston is then pushed back to its home position by the force of the springs in the
                     tool.

              M. It is recommended that the steps G, J, K and L, are repeated to ensure that the rolls are
                 securely locked onto the pinion shaft.

              N. Depress the red push button on the remote control box "PUSH TO STOP", this will
                 eliminate the possibility that the pump could be operated accidentally.

              O. Disconnect the hoses and remove the tool. Place the protective covers on both the hose
                 and tool hydraulic connections.

              Q. Fit the running cover retaining bolt and tighten.

   4.2        Roll Removal

              A. Release the entry and delivery side guides and move them back from the rolls.

              B. Release the running cover retaining bolt and remove the cover.

              C. Fit the removal tool onto the flange of the tapered sleeve. Ensure that the roll removal
                 tool is locked onto the flange. The spring pin located in the side of the removal tool
                 must be located against one of the protruding tabs on the flange of the tapered sleeve.
              D. Connect the hose to the nipple on the tool. Ensure the correct hose is used.

              E. Switch ON the pump unit at the front mounted ON \ OFF switch.

              F. Release the red push button marked “PULL TO START” on the pump unit remote
                 control box. Turn the switch to "DISMOUNT".

              G. Press the “DISMOUNT” button on the remote control box. The piston will be
                 pressurized and the tapered sleeve is pulled off of the shaft.

              H. RELEASE the button as soon as the tapered sleeve is loose, this will allow the spring in
                 the tool to push the piston back to its home position.

                   Note: Normally the operator will hear a slight cracking noise, as the taper between the
                   pinion shaft and the sleeve is broken, at the same moment the needle on the pressure
                   gauge will fall. It is at this point that the button is released.

              I.   If the operator continues to press the button, the pressure in the tool will push the piston
                   beyond its designed stroke, damaging the seals in the tool.

              J.   Depress the red push button on the remote control unit, marked "PUSH TO STOP", to
                   disable the unit.

              K. Remove the hose and disengage the removal tool. Place the protective covers on both
                 the hose and tool hydraulic connections.

              L. Remove the roll and sleeve assembly together. Place the roll assembly onto a protected
                 surface, or directly on to the roll transport. Remove any spacers that may have been
                 used.

MAINTENANCE

IMPORTANT: Always isolate, shutoff and/or disconnect Water, Air, Hydraulic and Electrical
power supply sources before performing any repairs or maintenance. Read Safety Instructions and
Warnings for each system and component prior to working on machinery. Read and refer to Safety
section of this manual before performing and maintenance or repairs.
Make sure the Mill process stations and pass line has been completely shut down and interlocks are
working properly. All Safety Devices must be properly maintained and never bypassed to assure the
safety of the operators.
WARNING: The Pinch Roll Assembly is potentially dangerous and capable of inflicting severe
                 bodily injuries and fatal electric shock. Before starting any Maintenance task,
                 comply with all company policies relating to safety. Also, be thoroughly familiar
                 with the general safety requirements.

WARNING: ALWAYS WEAR HEAT RESISTANT GLOVES WHEN CHANGING GUIDE EQUIPMENT.

WARNING: HOT PRODUCT TRAVELLING THROUGHOUT THE MILL CAN MAKE ALL EQUPIMENT
SURFACES A HIGH TEMPERATURE CONDITION AND CAUSE INJURY.       CONSIDER ALL
SURFACES THROUGHOUT THE MILL AS HOT!!

MAINTENANCE RECORDING
The principal maintenance problems that occur with rolling mills are the result of conditions that develop
slowly, taking many months to reach the trouble stage. Avoid potential maintenance troubles by keeping
records and acting on them.
Lube oil system maintenance is extremely important since the useful life of the oil film bearings, which
support the roll shafts, depends mostly on the cleanliness of the lubricating oil. These bearings rapidly wear
out and seize with contaminated lube oil. This has been especially true of the front Cleveite bearings on
previous mills.
IMPORTANT: REFER TO FLUIDS MAINTENANCE MANUAL FOR INFORMATION FOR
LUBRICATION AND COOLING SYSTEMS.

PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE INSTRUCTIONS
INTRODUCTION
Routine and Preventive Maintenance of the pinch roll assembly is required to ensure extended and proper
operation. Table 4 is provided as a quick reference guide for frequent periodic maintenance requirements
for the Pinch Roll assembly. Refer to the General Maintenance section of this manual and to the applicable
manufacturer’s technical manual for maintenance requirements and procedures of specific components of
Pinch Roll Assembly. Refer to Morgan assembly drawings as a guide and for additional information.

DEFINITION

Preventative maintenance is routine maintenance that, if performed as scheduled, helps to keep the pinch
roll assembly in good operating condition. Its primary purpose is to reduce the incidence of operating
failures, which require costly downtime for repairs. The recommended scheduled and planned
maintenance procedures below represent the anticipated minimum requirements for maintaining the pinch
rolls. As you accumulate operating experience, it may be feasible to reduce the frequency of checks and
inspections, however, do not reduce the lubrication frequency.

IMPORTANT

Always isolate shutoff and/or disconnect water, air, hydraulic and electrical power supply sources
before performing any repairs or maintenance. Read Safety Instructions and Warnings for each system
and component prior to working on machinery. Refer to safety section of this manual.
SCHEDULED AND PLANNED MAINTENANCE
1.0    Introduction
       The objectives of scheduled and planned maintenance programs are to maintain the mill in
       a state of optimum readiness and performance and to ensure continued high production
       rates. To gain these objectives, the Maintenance Department should develop and prepare
       a periodic sequence of inspections and preventive maintenance procedures for the mill and
       its supporting systems. The objective of corrective maintenance is to return equipment to
       operational status as quickly as possible following a malfunction. Replacing faulty parts
       with spare new or refurbished parts and the mill back to full operation best does this.

       The most important single factors conducive to maximum mean-time-between-failure are
       lubrication and cooling. Consequently, the most important task of preventive maintenance
       is to ensure a clean and adequate supply of lube oil at all times while the mill is running
       and to frequently lubricate those points which require grease lubrication, and keep the
       cooling system functioning properly.

       Based on many years of experience in the development and manufacture of rod and bar mills,
       Morgan Construction Company has developed a set of scheduled maintenance activities to
       provide guidance to the Maintenance Department in developing and implementing a planned
       maintenance program of their own.
2.0    Recommended Scheduled Maintenance
       Table 4 provides information to be used as a general guide for scheduling routine maintenance for
       the mill system and its associated components. This information represents the anticipated
       minimum for maintaining the mill system. For specific component operation and maintenance,
       refer to the manufacturer’s technical manual.

        2.1     Pinch Rolls, Bearings, Roll Holders and Seals

        Periodically replacing the roll shaft seals, Clevite bearings and Duplex bearings helps to eliminate
        more extensive repairs.
        Use the following methods for inspection of the rolls, bearings and shaft seals:
                A. Make periodic inspections of rolls.
                B. Take weekly in-the-mill lift test for every roll shaft and record the results. Use the lift
                   test to determine if the Duplex bearings are deteriorating. The lift tests also will
                   determine if the deterioration warrants removal of the pinch roll for rebuilding.
                       Whenever the mill is in operation be on the alert for oil leaking from roll necks,
                       indicating a defective seal. A drip would be tolerable, possibly indicating an
                       accumulation of oil in the flinger. Frequently check the water leg sight glass in the lube
                       oil drain piping. Signs of water in the lube oil system indicate a defective roll neck seal.
                       Replace defective seals immediately to prevent contaminating the mill lube oil system.

                       All roll shaft seals must be replaced on a regular schedule. An interval of 3 to 6 months
                       is not uncommon. Such practices demonstrate the importance of preventing cooling
                       water into the lube oil system.

              C.   SHAFT SEALS
              One source of lube oil contamination is roll cooling water. A defective roll shaft seal
              will allow roll cooling water, carrying scale and grime, into the lube oil system.

              Regularly inspect for signs of water in the lube oil system. If the laying head is served by
              the same oil system, it is also a possible source of the water, but usually the roll shaft
              seals are at fault. To help in detecting faulty seals, each stand should have a water leg
              glass in the lube oil return line. If there is any sign of water in one of these glasses,
              replace the seals of that stand.

              Common practice at several other mills is to have all roll shaft seals replaced after a
              certain length of time in the mill. At one mill in particular, the time interval is every
              three months. Such practices demonstrate the importance attached to keeping cooling
              water out of the oil system.

              D.   PINCH ROLL PERIODIC INSPECTION
              To prevent pinch roll breakdown, remove the pinch roll and disassemble for inspection in the
              maintenance shop. Inspect all components of the pinch roll. Pay particular attention to the
              Clevite bearings. The greatest threat to roll housing breakdown is seizure of the work side
              Clevite bearings. As mentioned before, the cause of Clevite deterioration is invariably
              contaminated lube oil. If the bearings are only polished and have but a scattering of fine
              surface scratches, the oil lube system is effective.

              E.    EXAMINING CLEVITE BEARINGS TO JUDGE OIL CONDITION

              When the oil is very clean, there is very little wearing of the Clevite bearings. The thin
              Babbitt overlay is just polished, making the surface in the contact area more reflective.
              There will probably be a number of fine scratches in the surface. The life of the Clevites
              with such a lubricating system is unlimited.

              In contrast, Clevites have been removed from mills with contaminated oil and the bearings
              are worn into the copper lead layer. Another sign of a contaminated lube oil system is deep
              surface score marks all the way into the copper. The Clevite bearings in these mills are
              wearing out and should be replaced frequently. More to the point, the lube oil system should
              be cleaned.

              An examination of the material attached to the magnetic plugs in the roll housings will give
              additional evidence of oil condition. In six months time, the build-up should be no more
              than slight sludge. If there are large abrasive particles, the lube oil system is contaminated.

              One sign that the lube oil system is becoming contaminated is the time between filter
              cleanings. The reasons for the increased contamination can be too much water, low oil
              level in the main tank, poor filter cleaning practice, failure to run the oil purifying
              system, or a combination of these faults.

        AXIAL LIFT TEST PROCEDURE

        This test requires the removal of the rolls and the tapered sleeves. A special lifting tool is installed
        on the end of the roll shaft to be tested. (Refer to Morgan assembly drawing and Figures 8 and 9 as a
        guide.

              1.     Remove the roll and tapered sleeve assembly.

              2.     Install the angle brackets and lifting bar onto the ends of the roll shafts. It may be
                     helpful to loosely assemble the above parts to the roll shafts and then tighten the cap
                     screws. The lift bar will prevent the angles from turning out of position during bolt
                     tightening.

              3.     Using a "Starret" last word dial indicator or equivalent, that is attached to adjustable
                     posts and supported by a magnetic base. Position the contact point at some point on
                     the shaft near the areas shown on Inspection Chart. The contact point must exert
                     force on the area to preload the dial indicator allowing reading in both upward and
                     downward directions. With the dial preloaded, set the indicator reading at zero.

              4.     With the dial indicator set at zero, manually apply force to the lifting bar with a
                     torque wrench in an upward direction and note the indicator reading; then set the
                     indicator back to zero and manually apply force to the lifting tool in a downward
                     direction, again noting the indicator reading. The total of these readings is the end
                     play for the roll shaft.

              5.     Record the reading on the Inspection Record Chart and compare with the original
                     data recorded. If the increase in end play, when compared to the original end play
                     exceeds 0.10 mm (.004 inch), move the pinch roll to the Maintenance Shop for
                     rebuild/overhaul.

NOTE: Test the other roll shaft. Move the dial indicator to the other shaft and set as previously described.
      Apply axial lift and record the reading on the historical data SHEET and compare with original data
      recorded.

       2.2    Motors
              Inspect for unusual heat and noise conditions.
       2.3    Couplings
              The maintenance technician should inspect all mill couplings for erratic operation and
              unusual noise daily. Most couplings are of the sealed lubrication type. Refer to the
              manufacturer’s literature for applicable maintenance information to the specific coupling.

       2.4    Breathers and Filters
              Every three months, or sooner if conditions warrant, remove the breathe/filter element and
              clean it in a suitable solvent. Air dry thoroughly and then reinstall. Replace filter element
              if necessary.

       2.5    Entry and Delivery Guides
              At least once a day, check oil level in receiving tanks/reservoirs of the air-oil systems.
              Refill tank/reservoir if necessary. Do not overfill. Monitor the air and oil consumption of
              the guides to ensure proper lubrication.
       2.6    Guard Covers
              Most guard covers require very little maintenance. After every closure check to see that
              cover is properly seated and secure. Check all connections for leaks and tightness.
              Lubricate jack and pivot pins.
       2.7    Piping
              Once a week, inspect all piping lengths, flanges and mounting for cracks and excessive
              wear and replace as necessary.

       2.8    Hoses and Connections
              Inspect hoses daily for any leaks, cuts or abrasions and replace if necessary. Check
              connections for any leaks and tighten or replace if necessary.
       2.9    Mounting Hardware
              Check all mounting hardware throughout entire system for tightness and defects. Tighten
              fasteners as required. Refer to manufacturer technical manuals for any torque
              requirements.

3.0    Planned Corrective Maintenance
Required maintenance for specific components of the mill system may differ dramatically from each
manufacturer specifications. However, listed below are general maintenance procedures that should be
performed when any component or its subassemblies are dismantled for repairs. Refer to manufacturer’s
literature for more detailed operation and maintenance instructions for each specific component.
       3.1 General Maintenance Steps and Procedures
               A.     Cleaning: Clean all parts with a suitable solvent (mineral spirits, SAVASOL No. 5,
                      or equivalent) to remove scale, grease, grime or dirt. Use lint-free rags; do not use
                      cotton waste. Air dry after cleaning.
       WARNING: SOLVENTS USED FOR CLEANING CAN BE HARMFUL. FOLLOW THE
       SOLVENT MANUFACTURER'S RECOMMENDED SAFETY PROCEDURES FOR
       CLOTHING, VENTILATION AND FIRST AID.
       WARNING: Petroleum based solvents are flammable and their vapors are harmful.
       CAUTION: Be absolutely sure to maintain a clean environment during disassembly/re-
       assembly of all mill components. Dirt, scale or other foreign matter can have serious adverse
       affects on closely tolerance, precision equipment as well as contaminate the mill lube oil
       system.
               B.     Housekeeping - To the extent possible, keep all service areas clean. Do not allow
                      oil, grease, water or dirt to accumulate on floors and/or around units undergoing
                      repair, not only for the reasons stated above, but also for personnel safety.
               C.     Bearing and Sealing Surfaces - Inspect bearing and sealing surfaces closely for signs
                      of wear, nicks, scratches, gouges and build-up of scale or other foreign substances.
                      Remove light scratches, gouges and scale by polish grinding the surfaces as long as
                      design tolerances are not exceeded. Deep gouges and nicks may require resurfacing,
                      machining and grinding to restore the units to their original condition and
                      dimensions.
               D.     Oil Seals and Gaskets - Discard all O-rings and gaskets removed or disturbed during
                      disassembly and replace with new ones.
               E.     Internal Oil Passages - Pressure flush all internal oil passages and blow out the
                      passages with compressed air.
               F.     Internal Coolant Passages - Clean all internal coolant passages to loosen scale,
                      oxides or other contaminants that could impede or block passage of coolant. After
                      cleaning, pressure flush and blow out with compressed air. Use a special cylindrical
                      wire brush for cleaning passages.
               G.     Pre-lubrication prior to Re-assembly - Lubricate all gears, bushings, bearings and
                      seals with oil from the mill system before reassembling.

               H.     Aligning Parts during Re-assembly - Use guide studs during reinstallation of covers,
                      retainers and/or housings to ensure bolt hole and/or dowel pin alignment.



By Morgan Construction Co.                                                                                  Page 36
15 Belmont Street, Worcester, MA 01605                                                                        Rev A

               I.     Rigging Parts for Removal/Replacement - Many parts in the mill are too heavy to be
                      manhandled. Provide adequate rigging for lifting and supporting heavy parts before
                      attempting to dismantle or reassemble.
               J.   Sealing Compounds - Use sealing compounds regularly. Use caution to avoid
                    introducing compound into drain holes or passages where it might ultimately
                    contaminate the lube system.
WARNING: ADHESIVES MAY BE FLAMMABLE AND THEIR VAPORS HARMFUL.
               K. Strictly maintain water, oil, hydraulic and pneumatic integrity of the rolling mill.
                  Ensure that all personnel report any leakage immediately to the maintenance technician
                  for evaluation. Repair any leakage no matter how small, whether it is water, oil,
                  hydraulic fluid or air, immediately. Ignoring any leakage could cause mill shutdown
                  and, more importantly, injury or death to personnel. When inspecting, repairing or
                  reassembling any part of the mill ensure that sealing integrity is strictly observed
                  wherever necessary. Use sealing compound, such as Permatex, Tite-seal, or equivalent,
                  to obtain sealing integrity.
               L. Torque Requirements – Always torque all bolts and fasteners in accordance with latest
                  reference drawings and manufacturer’s specifications. Refer to torque specifications
                  table at the end of this manual for additional standard torque values
       3.2 Bearings
           Ball and roller bearings are not repairable. Either they are good and suitable for reuse or they
           are no good and must be replaced

CAUTION: Because a used bearing may be defective without the defect being visually evident, during
any maintenance task, replace all bearings removed from their respective shafts with new bearings.
NOTE: For ease of installation of bearings, adhere to the following guidelines and procedures:
       A. Observe a "NO SUBSTITUTION" policy because of the special design requirement for these
          bearings.
       B. New bearings are packed with rust-preventive grease (or other protective coating) and wrapped
          in grease-resistant paper before they are shipped. Do not unwrap bearings until time for
          installation. Then, unwrap and thoroughly wash the new bearing and air dry. Pre-lubricate
          immediately with oil from the mill system.
       C. When pressing a bearing on or off a shaft, do not apply pressure to the outer race. Use a bearing
          installation tool whenever possible. Apply pressure only to the race that is a tight fit.
       D. Installation of large bearings is simplified by heating the bearing in clean oil to a temperature
          of 250°F (120°C) maximum. Do not exceed this temperature. Allow sufficient time to ensure
          that the bearing is heated throughout. This will sufficiently expand the bearing and allow it to
          slide easily over the shaft to its proper location. Take care to prevent cocking of the inner race
          as this may cause the bearing to seize before it is properly seated.
           Heat the bearings at a maximum temperature of 120°C (250°F) in oil for1 hour minimum, or in
           an electric furnace for 1-1/2 hours minimum, or by electric induction for 15 minutes minimum.

       Unless the oil seals are leaking, couplings require very little maintenance other than lubrication.

       3.4 Shaft and Coupling Shields
               A. For protection of mill personnel, shield all exposed rotating couplings (the drive motor to
                  drive housing floating shaft coupling) whenever the mill is running.

                       SHUT DOWN.

CORRECTIVE MAINTENANCE INSTRUCTIONS
Corrective maintenance encompasses those repair procedures required to return the Pinch Roll assembly to
satisfactory operating condition. Such repairs do not necessarily return the equipment to like new condition.
Rather, the objective is to make it operational again as soon as possible. It is recommended to replace faulty
parts/components and sub-assemblies with new or previously refurbished spare parts/components and sub-
assemblies. Those parts removed may then be refurbished or reconditioned after the main equipment has
been returned to service.
IMPORTANT
Always isolate, shutoff and/or disconnect Water, Air, Hydraulic and Electrical power supply sources
before performing any repairs or maintenance. Read Safety Instructions and Warnings for each system
and component prior to working on machinery. Refer to Safety section in this manual.
INTRODUCTION
Corrective Maintenance of the Pinch Rolls as defined above, is intended to keep down time at a minimum by
replacing components and then dismantling and overhauling the removed component in a service area away
from the mill. Once refurbished, the component becomes a spare shelf part, ready to be utilized as a
replacement when needed. Removal procedures are given herein of components being replaced.

Components that require overhaul/refurbishment should be maintained in accordance with the
manufacturer’s instructions. Refer to the manufacturers technical manual for maintenance and torque
requirements and procedures of specific components.
General guidelines and maintenance criteria are provided below when corrective maintenance of a
component or sub-assembly is required. These are minimum guidelines and should be used in conjunction
to the specific maintenance requirements from the component manufacturer. Upon re-assembly, tighten all
bolts, screws, nuts and fasteners in accordance with Morgan reference drawings torque requirements.
Torque specific components in accordance with the manufacturer’s requirements.

WARNING: Before performing any maintenance on mill equipment, shutoff or disconnect all power
supply sources. De-energize, dissipate and exhaust any stored energy from components. Restrain and
secure any moving parts of a component or system that could cause injury.

WARNING: The Pinch Roll Assembly is potentially dangerous and capable of inflicting severe
bodily injuries and fatal electric shock. Before starting any maintenance task, comply with all
company policies relating to safety. Also, be thoroughly familiar with the general requirements
1.0     General Maintenance Criteria
The following is a list of maintenance actions to perform whenever dismantling equipment for repairs.
        1.1     Electric controls and power cables -- Before disconnecting any wiring that does not have
                plug-in connectors, make sure that color coding is clearly identifiable or tag each wire
                carefully for reference at re-assembly.

        1.2     Rigging parts for removal/replacement -- Many parts that make up this equipment are much
                too heavy to be handled by one person. Provide adequate rigging for lifting and supporting
                heavy parts before attempting to dismantle any equipment. Note: Only trained personnel
                should remove, secure and rig components for lifting.

       1.3    Cleaning -- Clean all parts with a suitable solvent (mineral spirits, SAVASOL no.5, or
              equivalent) to remove all scale, grease, grime, or dirt. Use a clean wiper; do not use cotton
              waste. Air dry after cleaning.

       1.4    Bearings and Sealing Surfaces -- Closely inspect bearings and sealing surfaces for signs of
              wear, nicks, scratches, gouges, or build-up of scale or other foreign substances. Replace
              bearings that show any signs of deterioration. Scrape bushings slightly, being careful not
              to exceed the tolerance limits.

              To clean roller bearings, soak in clean solvent long enough to loosen any sludge, then
              gently slosh each bearing around near the top of the container to dislodge all pockets of
              grease. Scrub away stubborn accumulations with a small brush that has bristles that do not
              break off. Do not spin dirty bearings, but rotate races slowly while washing and
              scrubbing.

              Rinse the bearings in clean solvent and air dry. Hold both races when blowing with clean,
              dry compressed air. Do not allow the air jet to spin the bearing; rather, turn each race by
              hand to expose all surfaces to the drying air. If the bearing is to be stored for later reuse,
              wrap it in wax paper or other grease-proof wrapping.
              CAUTION: A bearing may be defective without the defect being visually evident:
              replace any bearing removed during any maintenance task with new or cleaned bearing at
              re-assembly. New bearings are packed with rust-preventative grease (or other protective
              coating) and wrapped in grease-resistant paper before they are shipped. Do not unwrap
              the bearing until time for installation. Unwrap and thoroughly wash the new bearing and
              air dry. Pre-lubricate immediately with Mobil 525 (or equivalent).

              NOTE: For ease of installation of bearings, heat the bearings at a maximum temperature
              of 121°C (250°F) in oil for one hour minimum, or in an electric furnace for 1-1/2 hours
              minimum, or by bearing induction heater for 15 minutes minimum.
       1.5    Oil Seals – Replace (Mandatory Replacement) all seals, o-rings and gaskets that are
              removed or disturbed during disassembly procedure. Make sure seals and o-rings seat
              properly upon re-assembly.

       1.6    Oil Passages -- Pressure flush oil passages and blow dry with compressed air.
       1.7    Pre-lubrication Prior to Re-assembly -- Lightly lubricate all seals, bearings, bushings, and
              gears with oil before installation.

       1.8    Aligning Parts During Re-assembly -- Because of the weight of large parts, use guide
              studs during re-assembly to ensure proper bolt hole and /or dowel pin alignment.

       1.9    Clean all parts and inspect for scratches, cracks, burrs, flaking, pitting, scaling or
              discoloration of mating or load-bearing surfaces.

       1.10   Hand scrape any bushings that have not become out-or-round to remove burrs, small
              scratches or accumulated foreign substances. Replace any bushing showing gross
              deformation or cracking.

       1.11   Check shafts and pivot pins for straightness with v-blocks and dial indicator. It is possible
              to straighten bent shafts in a hydraulic press, but if spares are available, it is much better to

              only if no spares are available, but replace them whenever possible.

       1.12   If roller bearing surfaces become badly worn, rough, pitted, scaled or blistered, dress them
              on a lathe or grind them clean as long as the design tolerances are met.

2.0    Pinch Roll Removal From Mill

       2.1    Disconnect and remove all necessary external components that will obstruct the lifting of the
              pinch roll assembly including all air, hydraulic and electrical connections.

              A.    De-energize the power and control circuits to the pinch roll.

              B.     Isolate the air, water and lube oil lines from their respective mill supply and
                     discharge systems and disconnect the piping. Disconnect all lube oil and drain
                     connections. Block and plug all piping and drains to prevent entrance of dirt and
                     contamination.

              C.    Remove the coupling guard.

              D.    Disconnect the coupling flange bolts and slide the coupling sleeves back on their
                    shafts. Cover exposed parts to prevent dirt and grime from entering.

              F.    Remove the cover and rotary actuator as described in Component Removal Section
                    3.1D. Remove Cover Assembly as a complete unit.

              G.    Remove the hardware securing the pinch rolls to its support base/foundation.

              H.    Rig and secure pinch roll assembly for removal. Use lifting points (pads) on
                    housing assembly. See Figure 10 as a guide.

              Note: More than one housing section may be removed together. Make sure crane has
              sufficient lifting capacity.

              I.      Remove pinch roll assembly to shop area for maintenance.

3.0    Component Removal
       3.1    The procedures below are for removing components and sub-assemblies from the pinch
              roll that may require overhaul/refurbishment and reinstalling new or refurbished parts
              on the mill floor. Part removal should be only to the extent needed to repair and
              refurbish components.

             Note: To help prevent dirt and contamination entering into the Pinch Roll Assembly,
             dismantling and removal of parts should only be to the extent needed to remove the
             desired component or subassembly. Always cover exposed parts to prevent dirt and
             grime from entering.
              A.    GUIDES (RECEIVING AND DELIVERY)
                      NOTE: Guide Assemblies consist of two guide halves.
                      1.  Turn off the cooling water and Lube supplies to the pinch rolls and delivery
                          guides.
                      2.  Manually open the cover shielding the rolls and guides. Pin the
                          cover in place using the pins and stops.
                      3.  Loosen the clamps holding each guide assembly.
                      4.  Remove the pair of guide halves.
                      5.  Thoroughly clean the inner surface of the guide halves and mating surface of
                          the guide support. Remove all traces of contaminants. Blow out the passages
                          with compressed air. Ensure that the inner surfaces of the guide halves are
                          smooth and free of scale, nicks, or burrs. Polish as necessary.
                      6.  Reassemble and install the guide assembly in reverse sequence.

                            NOTE: The receiving and delivery guides vary depending upon the rods
                            being processed. Align the applicable guide assembly to the roll grooves using
                            a guide alignment tool.
              B.    ROLLS
                      1.  Turn off the cooling water supplies to the pinch rolls.

                       2.     Manually open the cover shielding the rolls and guides. Pin the
                              cover in place using the pins and stops.

             NOTE: Remove the splash guard from the cover before opening the cover.
                       3.     Remove the receiving entry guide and delivery guide if required.
                       4.     Remove the locking nuts and running covers from the ends of the roll shafts.
                       5.     Remove the rolls from the ends of the shafts. Refer to roll removal section.

       WARNING: BEFORE RETURNING POWER SYSTEMS TO SERVICE, ENSURE THAT
       ALL PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF EQUIPMENT BEING RETURNED TO SERVICE.
       CONTROLS MAY HAVE BEEN REPOSITIONED WHILE MAINTENANCE WAS
       BEING PERFORMED, CAUSING UNEXPECTED MOVEMENTS OF EQUIPMENT.
       After complying with the above WARNINGS, open the safety stop located in front of the
       pinch roll, return all power systems to service and remove all tags from the controls.

              C.     COUPLINGS
               Normally the worn out pinch roll coupling would be replaced when the pinch roll
               unit is moved for repairs. However, if the coupling must be replaced as an
               independent operation, follow the procedures below:

       Note: Coupling halves should be replaced as a set.
                1.    De-energize and lock out the electrical power supply and control circuits to
                      the pinch roll and its drive motor.
                2.    Remove the coupling guard.

                3.    Remove the drive motor, if necessary, following steps below.

                      a)     Tag, and then disconnect the electrical leads to the drive motor.

                      b)     Rig the motor for lifting.

                      c)     Remove the hardware connecting the coupling flanges.
                             Pull back the coupling flanges.

                      d)     Remove the hardware attaching the motor to its base, if necessary.

                      e)     Carefully lift the motor off its base and set it aside on wooden blocks
                             for reassembly.

                4.    Remove the nut and washer from the end of the motor shaft. Using a suitable
                      puller, pull the hub off the shaft. Remove the key.

                5.    Remove the coupling hub that fits on the pinch roll drive shaft by removing
                      the cotter pin, jam nut and flat washer from the shaft. Attach a suitable puller
                      to the shaft. As the puller is tightened, rap the hub sharply with a hammer so
                      that it will "pop" free of the shaft. Remove the key.

                6.    Clean all coupling parts and the shaft ends thoroughly. Carefully inspect the coupling
                      halves for signs of excessive wear. If possible, refurbish the coupling halves by
                      replacing all the seals and worn parts. If this is not possible, replace the coupling
                      halves.
                7.    Place the key in the motor coupling shaft.
                8.    Install the motor coupling half on the motor shaft. Secure in place with the nut and
                      washer removed at disassembly.

4.0      PINCH ROLL DISASSEMBLY (IN SHOP)
       4.1    Removal of External Components from Housing Assemblies.

              A.    Remove Breather.

              B.    Remove Cover Assembly, if still attached.

              C.    Remove the servo motor assembly if required.

              D.    Remove the receiving and delivery guides and guide supports as described in section 3.1A.

              E.    Remove the lock nuts and running covers from the ends of the shafts and remove the rolls
                    from the ends of the shafts as described in section 3.1B. See Roll Removal Section.

       4.2    Disassembly of Housings and Removal of Internal Components.

              A.      Remove the spacers from each of the roll shafts.

              B.      Lift the outer flinger off each of the roll shafts. Remove the O-ring from each
                      flinger. Replace with new O-rings at reassembly.

              C       Remove the roll shaft seal plate. Remove the seals from the seal plate and discard.
                      Replace them at reassembly.

              D.      Lift the inner flinger off each of the roll shafts. Remove the O-ring from each
                      flinger. Replace at reassembly.

              E.      Remove the front face plate from the pinch roll assembly.

              F.      From the drive side of housing, remove seal retainer from the input shaft. Remove
                      Seal plate with seal and wear sleeve from input shaft. Remove gasket from housing.
                      Remove the drive shaft bearing retainer and shims. Remove the seal and replace it at
                      reassembly. Inspect the shims and replace them, if necessary. Wire the shims
                      together and set aside for reassembly.


              G.      Rig the housing top for lifting. Take up the slack but do not strain. Remove all
                      attaching hardware from between the upper housing and the housing intermediate
                      section. Carefully hoist the upper housing straight up in the air to clear the upper
                      roller holder assembly and the idler shaft pinion. Set the housing top aside for
                      reassembly, on wooden blocks or other suitable mounting blocks.

              H.      Disconnect the internal lube piping from the upper roller holder assembly.

       4.3    DISMANTLING OF ROLLER HOLDER ASSEMBLY (Upper and Lower)

       Note: Disassembly steps for upper and lower roller assemblies are similar.

              A. Remove the Inner and outer bearing retainers and shims from each roll shaft drive side
                 bearing cartridge.
              B. Remove the bearing cartridge. Press the shaft assembly in toward the roll holder if necessary.
              C. Remove the roll shaft assembly out of the roller holder assembly through the work side
                 bore of the roller holder. Use care not to damage the gear teeth or the bearing cartridge
                 bore. The clearance between the gear teeth and the roller holder bore is close.
              D. Remove the retainer plate from the end of the shaft.
              E. Back off the setscrew in the bearing cartridge enough to allow for removal of the bearing
                 spray.
              F. Press the inner race of bearings from the shaft.
              G. Remove the ball bearings, bearing spacer and spray assembly from the bearing cartridge.
                  NOTE: The inner spacer and the spray ring are a matched set. If one or the other is
                  damaged, replace them both.
              H. Remove the locknuts and the lock washers from each end of the driven and input shaft.
              I. Remove bearing retainers and shims from drive side bearing cartridges. Remove the
                 bearing cartridge.
              J. Remove the attaching hardware from the face plate assembly.
              K. Rig and Secure face place separate from roll holder with shaft assembly still attached to
                  face plate.
              L. Remove the snap ring from the work side bearing cartridge.
              M. Press the idler shaft along with the face plate assembly from the drive side ball bearing.
              N. Back off the set screw in the bearing cartridges (work side and drive side) enough to
                  allow for removal of the bearing spray.
              O. Press the idler shaft out of the face plate assembly.
              P. Remove the spacer.
              Q. Remove the bearing and bearing spray from the bearing cartridge. Remove the bearing
                  spray seals. Replace with new seals at reassembly.
              R. Remove the bearing and bearing spray from the drive side bearing cartridge. Remove the
                  bearing spray seals. Replace them with new seals at reassembly.
              S. Clean and inspect the idler gear. Remove the gear only if necessary. If it is necessary to
                  remove the gear, heat the gear carefully and press it off the shaft.

        5.6    CLEVITES
               To assemble the clevite bearing halves in the roller holder face plates proceed as follows:
               A.     Heat the face plate to 121°C (250°F). Place the clevite bearing halves in dry ice while
                      the face plate is coming up to temperature.

               B.     Use a garter spring to hold the bearing halves together when starting the bearing in the
                      face plate bore.
      CAUTION: Note the location of the bearing plates and of the bearing half with the hole in it.
               C.     Press the bearing into the face plate until it reaches the shoulder.
               D.     Check the alignment of the bearing and oil hole.

        5.7    ROLL SHAFT LIFT TESTS AND PASSLINE SETTING

               Prior to reassembly of the front plate and seal plate the correct location of the roll shaft taper
               must be adjusted to establish the correct center line of pass.

6.0   Returning Equipment to Service

WARNING: BEFORE RETURNING POWER SYSTEMS TO SERVICE, INSURE THAT ALL
PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE EQUIPMENT BEING RETURNED TO SERVICE. CONTROLS
MAY HAVE BEEN REPOSITIONED WHILE MAINTENANCE WAS BEING PERFORMED, CAUSING
UNEXPECTED MOVEMENTS OF EQUIPMENT.

WARNING:    BEFORE STARTING ANY OF THE MILL EQUIPMENT, BE SURE ALL PERSONNEL
ARE AT THEIR WORK AREAS, OR IN THE AREAS THAT HAVE BEEN DESIGNATED AS SAFE
WHEN THE EQUIPMENT IS IN OPERATION. THE MILL OWNER AND HIS AUTHORIZED
SUPERVISOR OF OPERATING PERSONNEL ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR OBSERVING, INITIATING
AND ENFORCING THE OBSERVANCE OF THIS WARNING.

       Rotate the input shaft manually to confirm that there is nothing impeding the rotation of the
       shafts. Turn on the lubricating oil pumps and check for any blocked oil lines and make certain
       that the gear spray's coverage is correct.

       Check the lubrication inlet piping for leakage. Install the vent cover and its gasket.
       When starting to run the equipment after any assembly or maintenance has been carried out,
       always run the motor at a slow speed for a time and gradually increase the speed while listening
       for any unusual noise and checking the bearing temperatures. Investigate any questionable noise
       or other unusual occurrence before increasing the speed.

       WARNING: BEWARE OF PINCH POINTS. BLOCK AND RESTRAIN ROTATING

       WARNING: Do not exceed equipment ratings. Never attempt to press on or lift a load

       Never set the relief valve to a higher pressure than the maximum rated pressure of the pump.

       WARNING: The system operating pressure must not exceed the pressure rating of the lowest

       CAUTION: Avoid damaging connected hoses. Avoid sharp bends and kinks when routing
       hoses. Using a bent or kinked hose will cause severe back-pressure. Sharp bends and kinks
       will internally damage the hose leading to premature hose failure.


       Do not drop heavy objects on hose. A sharp impact may cause internal damage to hose wire
       strands. Applying pressure to a damaged hose may cause it to rupture. DO NOT lift or pull
       equipment by hoses or couplers. Rig and secure equipment for safe transport.

       CAUTION: Keep hydraulic equipment away from flames and heat. Excessive heat will soften
       packing and seals, resulting in fluid leaks. Heat also weakens hose materials and packings.
       For optimum performance do not expose equipment to temperatures of 65°C [150°F] or
       higher. Protect all hoses and cylinders from weld spatter and extreme heat.

       DANGER: Do not handle pressurized hoses. Escaping oil under pressure can penetrate the
       skin, causing serious injury. If oil is injected under the skin, see a doctor immediately.


       WARNING: Only use hydraulic cylinders in a coupled system. Never use a cylinder with
       unconnected couplers. If the cylinder becomes extremely overloaded, components can fail
       catastrophically causing severe personal injury. Never bleed system to exposed atmosphere.


       WARNING: Immediately replace worn or damaged parts.
       IMPORTANT: Qualified trained technicians must only service Mill equipment.

       WARNING: Do not use electric pumps in an explosive atmosphere. Adhere to all local and
       national electrical codes. Start the pump with the valve in the neutral position to prevent
       accidental cylinder operation. Keep hands clear of moving parts and pressurized hoses.

       CAUTION: To prevent damage to electric motors, check specifications. Use of incorrect

1.0     Safety Procedures

IMPORTANT: All Safety Devices must be properly maintained and never bypassed to assure the
safety of the operators.

Stock presents serious hazards and the nature of the hazards and rolling mill operating practices make the
elimination or control of these hazards extremely difficult. For operator control of the process and/or
product quality, the stock must be generally visible and accessible, yet be constrained to follow a
prescribed path. Any deviation from the path is referred to as a cobble. Cobbles occur at random times
and places and the direction taken by the cobbled stock is unpredictable. Cobbles are most frequently
caused by front ends failing to follow a prescribed path. Improper speed regulation, guide adjustment,
and stock temperature are also causes of cobbling anywhere along the length of a bar in process in the
rolling train. The following recommended guidelines will help to produce a quality product in a safe
manner.


        1.1     Visibility and Communications

        Visibility from a control point to machinery is an important safety consideration. Locations of
        pulpits and other control points should provide an optimum view of equipment controlled from
        that point.

                A. Where possible and practical, visibility should be realized by line-of-sight.

                B. Where line-of-sight visibility is impossible or impractical, a mirror with proper
                   lighting can be used provided that the immediate environment will not dirty or cloud
                   the reflective surface and that the mirror location does not make it liable to breakage.

        1.2     Audible Communications
                Intercoms, telephone, and radio communications can be used to supplement or as
                substitutes only when visual contact is not possible.

        1.3     Safety Stops

                Guide adjustments may be made only when the stand concerned is shut down.
                Mechanical or electrically operated stops must be used to block any stock from
                inadvertently entering into the mill.

                Make sure the mill is shut down and material can not run through the stand. Make sure
                that stops remain in place as long as personnel making adjustments are in the hazard area.
                For example, the snap shear will be closed ahead of the NTM.

       1.4    Alarms

              The alarms as described in the control specifications will have a warning system to alert
              the operators of a new oncoming front ends.

              A prominently located light board should be used with the warning system to indicate the
              strand in use and the progress of the stock in the mill.

       1.5    Restart - After a Housing Change, Roll Change, or Pass Change

              When a service operation is completed, the Mill must be restarted in the following
              sequence:

              1.       All mechanical stops will be moved.

              2.       All Guards will be in place.

              3.       All personnel will clear the hazardous area.

              4.       Permissive switches will be placed in “ALLOW RESTART” position and all
                       interlocks engaged.

              5.       Operators at control stations will be notified that the equipment may be restarted.

              6.       Operators must not restart the mill until they are completely satisfied that
                       restarting will not present hazards to personnel. An audible signal will be given
                       by the operator to indicate that restart is imminent.

2.0     Safety Shutoff and Lockout/Tagout

IMPORTANT: Operators must be familiar with all Main Pulpit and Local Control Station
switches, indicators and controls. Operators must also know where all power supply shutoff and
isolation locations are in the Water, Air, Hydraulic, Lubrication and Electrical Systems.

IMPORTANT: Always isolate, shutoff and/or disconnect Water, Air, Hydraulic and Electrical power
supply sources before performing any repairs, maintenance or roll and guide changes. Read Safety
Instructions and Warnings for each system and component prior to working on machinery. Read and
refer to Safety section of this manual before performing and maintenance or repairs.
Lockout and Tagout isolation valves located in the supply lines to the pinch roll before performing any
maintenance or repairs. Lockout and Tagout control switches at the Local Control Station and Main

Make sure the Mill process stations and pass line has been completely shut down and interlocks are

safety of the operators.
WARNING: The Laying Head Assembly is potentially dangerous and capable of inflicting severe
bodily injuries and fatal electric shock. Before starting any Maintenance task, comply with all
company policies relating to safety. Also, be thoroughly familiar with all safety requirements.

OPERATION

IMPORTANT: Always read safety instructions and warnings for each system and component prior
to operating and working on machinery. Refer to safety section for general safety steps and
procedures.

INTRODUCTION

There are two laying heads installed, one in each strand of this two strand mill.

The laying head assembly takes straight finished rod from the pinch rollers and transforms it into coiled
rings that are discharged onto the Stelmor conveyor for further processing. The laying head consists of a
spinning structure containing a spiral shaped path of piping to form and discharge the rod. The laying head
runs continuously during normal operation.

Each revolution of the laying head produces one ring on the cooling conveyor. The size of the ring is
determined by the length of rod passing through the Laying Head during the time required for one
revolution. The distance the conveyor travels during one revolution of the laying head determines the offset
between successive rings being placed on the conveyor.

The Laying Head is designed for manual and automatic operation. The Operating Stations (Main Pulpit and
Local) help test, monitor and adjust conditions that may occur through the automated system. Refer to Table
1 for a description of the electrical equipment used in the Laying Head assembly.

COMPONENTS

1.0    Laying Head Assembly Refer to Figures 1 through 6 as a reference guide.

       1.1     Operation

       The motor’s calibrated speed is regulated to follow the RSM rod delivery speed. Control shall
       always limit laying head minimum speed reference to 95% of rod delivery speed due to mechanical
       interference from resulting oversize ring.

       The Laying head motor Speed Pulse Generator is used for speed regulation (mounted at non-drive
       end) and is also used for the laying head position encoder system. The encoder system is electronic
       program logic controlled and is required to exactly match main drive gear ratio. Overspeed
       protection is provided in the PLC software and also by a motor mounted Overspeed switch. The
       overspeed switch is a MANDATORY SAFETY DEVICE, and no substitution is allowed such as
       electronically monitoring a pulse generator or encoder. Shutdown is set at 1306 motor rpm, which
       equates to approximately _____ m/sec laying head speed.

       Note: The overspeed protection must be set to shut down at 5% over the top rated mill
       operating speed. Verify this feature before coupling the motor.

          A. Safety Guard Hood

          The Safety Hood is closed during normal operation and opened when performing maintenance.
          Refer to Interlock Section. The Safety Guard Hood is operated by hydraulic valve unit with a 2.2
          kW motor.

          The safety hood is opened and closed by a rotary hydraulic actuator controlled by Cover
          Open/Close double solenoid, 3-position valve. The following sequence shall be used to operate
          the cover up or down.

          1. When the operator is pressing cover up/down the electrical motor will start.

          2. After a 0.5 s time delay (to build up pressure) the valve is operated to selected position.

          3. When pushbutton is re-leased, the 2.2 kW electrical motor will stop

          Hood Position proximity switches indicate open and closed positions.

          Safety latches are set manually.

          The following safety guard hood interlocks are required:

          1. The laying head drive is allowed to operate only when the guard is fully lowered, as
             signaled by the proximity switch.

          2. The guard cannot be raised while the laying head drive is running.

          3. The guard cannot be raised unless the snap shear ahead of NTM® is closed. Also, the snap
             shear cannot be opened unless the laying head guard is fully closed.

          Never perform maintenance to the laying head with only the safety stop holding the cover. The
          hydraulic system is intended to assist in opening the cover and not as a safety device.

          WARNING: CONSIDER ALL MILL EQUIPMENT AS POTENTIALLY HAZARDOUS AT ALL
          TIMES. IT IS CAPABLE OF CRUSHING ANY BODY PART CAUGHT IN IT.

          B. Tail End Speed Up

          The Tail End Speed Up functions to speed up larger, slower speed products to provide
          sufficient energy for the rod tail end to clear the laying head.
          C. Wobble Control

          This Control cycles the laying head speed relative to the finished rod speed that produces varying
          ring diameters. The Wobble Control is used primarily on coarse/large size rod to allow the rings
          to nest better when they form in the reform tub. The Wobble is applied after the front end of rod
          coil is on the conveyor and is removed before the tail end arrives on the conveyor. The wobble
          rate permits full plus/minus 100% torque swings at all speeds, but prevents swing above 100%
          torque at any speed. Maximum limits of plus 10% and minus 5% speed are used.

          D. Drive System Stabilization

          Special closed loop stabilization circuits and open loop lead (phase advance) circuits are used to
          compensate for the following conditions:

               1. The laying head load inertia is several times more than motor inertia.

               2. There is some backlash in the gearing between the laying head and motor.

               3. During wobble control, the motor torque passes through zero frequently.

               4. The laying head must follow a rapid speed change during tail end speed up.

          Note: Crossover frequency above 2 radians per second may cause oscillation in backlash zone.
          Lead network in speed reference circuit is used to overcome slow speed regulator response.

          E. Bottom Tripper Control

          Both side and bottom ring trippers are used to aid in the control and delivery of the coil rings
          from the laying head to the conveyor. The tripper plates are controlled and adjusted by a manual
          hand crank wheel attached to a gear reducer.

          F. Unbalance Detector

          The purpose of the unbalance detector is primarily for worker protection. The laying head may
          self-destruct if the rotor becomes unbalanced. The unbalance detector consists of the unbalance
          pickup and the unbalance monitor. The system is designed to indicate peak velocity in the
          horizontal, cross-position direction.

          The Unbalance Pickup is a seismic velocity transducer and is located on the side of the Laying
          Head gear housing. The Unbalance Monitor that analyzes transducer signal is a panel mounted
          device with a power supply/relay board. The monitor display should be calibrated for 15
          mm/sec peak velocity.

          The monitor should be mounted in the drive panel for the laying head. Refer to the
          manufacturer’s manual for initial setup of the unit. Instructions are provided for wiring, single
          channel selection, alarm delay, startup delay, and alarm trip set points.

          Two set points for alarm (Alert) and shutdown (Danger) are utilized as follows:

               Alarm    = 7 mm/s rpk (mm/sec peak velocity calculated).
               Shutdown = 10 mm/s rpk (mm/sec peak velocity calculated).

          The signal for shutdown must be active 5 seconds before shutdown occurs. A 5 second delay
          timer is contained within the unbalance monitor unit.

          G. Front End Orientation onto Conveyor. Refer to Figures 1 and 2 for typical control
             configurations.

          The Laying Head speed is automatically adjusted to orient the rod front end so that it lies in a
          trailing mode to prevent snagging as it travels up the Stelmor conveyor.

          Coarse control starts when C&D shear knives are at zero cut position. Fine control starts when the
          front end is at NTM Exit HMD.

          Laying head speed is either boosted or retarded to obtain the correct position. The required
          accuracy is +/- 60 degrees max.

          At any point in its rotation the laying head position can be determined by use of a counter
          monitoring the pulse generator located at the back of the motor. Since the laying head is driven
          via a gear increaser, digital logic is used to relate the motor position to the head position.

          Once per laying head revolution a signal is generated from the Home Position proximity switch.
          A target rotating with the laying head activates this switch. When the laying head is started up
          from rest, the home position resets the pulse counter. Once reset, the home position signal is
          ignored and laying head position is determined only by the pulse counter.

          The laying head is indicated in a known, or Home position once per revolution by a Home
          Position proximity switch. The home position is used as a reference after the control system is
          powered up.

          When running, the counter is automatically set to zero every time the motor completes 39
          revolutions; this equates to the laying head having made exactly 67 revolutions and is back to
          the zero position. For every 39 motor rotation cycles, the head position is tracked by the pulse
          counter.

           H. Lubrication

           Correct lube pressure must be maintained to operate the laying head drive. The Lube Pressure
           switch initiates an alarm if pressure is not correct. Correct lube pressure is a permissive
           requirement to start the laying head.

           A LOW lube pressure causes the following to occur:

                   After the laying head is running and a LOW pressure condition occurs, a 0.5 second time
                   delay is initiated. If the LOW pressure condition is present after the time delay ends, the
                   following functions take place:

                   1.    The "scrap cut" mode for the crop and divide shear at the entry to the NTM is
                         initiated to divert the stock to the scrap chopping shear.

                   2.     A timer (adjustable from 0-3 seconds) is started which initiates the closing of the
                         snap shear at the entry side of the NTM.

                   3.    Once product has cleared the pinch roll and laying head as indicated by the tracking
                         system, the laying head drive is fast stopped.

           I.   Air Purge

           The Air Purge initiates a blast of air to the laying head pipe to remove sludge, scale and water
           deposited by the rod. The air purge is controlled by the Air Purge single solenoid valve.

           The air purge should start 5 seconds before the front end of the rod enters the laying head and
           remains on for 15 seconds. If the billet gaps are less than 5 seconds, the purge will come on
           while the tail end is still in the laying head and remain on during the billet gap and as the new
           front end passes through the laying head. Thus any scale that falls off the pipe as the front end is
           threaded is purged from the pipe.

           J. Air Wipe

           An Air wipe strips water from rod before entering laying head. The Air wipe is controlled by
           Air Wipe single solenoid valve and is energized whenever laying head is running.

          K. Water Cooling

          A water cooling jacket is used around the center pipe to insulate the main bearings from the heat of
          the traveling bar. This water is controlled by Cooling Water single solenoid valve. Water is
          turned on by energizing the solenoid whenever the laying head drive is running.

          Water mist spray cools the laying head cover. The water and air supplies are both controlled by
          single solenoid valves (Hood Mist Water and Hood Mist Air). The solenoids are energized to
          turn on the cooling sprays whenever the laying head drive is running.

          The Cooling Water Pressure Switch indicates correct water cooling pressure. Incorrect water
          pressure signals an alarm and stops billet delivery. The mill can be cleared of the existing product
          without cobble cutting.

          The pressure switch signal is ignored for 5 seconds whenever the laying head drive is started.

          L. Television/Monitor

          A camera is mounted above the entry tilt section of the conveyor, while a monitor is located in
          main control pulpit to give a close-up view of ring formation.

          The camera is located above the hot rings on the conveyor and therefore must be protected from
          the extreme heat. Wiring for the camera must be suitable for the high temperature conditions.

          If TV Water Flow switch indicates cooling water failure for 5 seconds, an alarm is activated. A
          stop rolling signal (Optional) can be initiated when the alarm is activated in order to avoid loss
          of the camera.
